scope: Initial eager-stats and final lazy-stats binaries are distinguished; isolated single-machine original-product RPC fault fixtures, not TPS or production acceptance.
final_lazy_stats_node_reverification: Both final-offline and final-aab passed; earlier failures and initial passes remain separate evidence.

cases.phase: propagate beyond global capacity before TTL
cases.finding: One offline recipient retained all eight global outbox entries despite healthy-peer credits, preventing the next batch before the unchanged eight-second deadline.

cases.phase: online quorum finality (offline node excluded from observation, not validator set)
cases.finding: The propagation gate passed, but the original aggregate receipt-wait window expired before the last two transactions finalized. This failed attempt is retained; the later diagnostic run does not establish the complete cause of this attempt.
A repeat passed the unchanged original receipt budget, including offline-node catch-up, four original-process cold restarts, successor transactions and archived quorum checks.

progress_analysis.measurement: Minimum published height across the three online nodes; reset the interval only on its increase. Sample time begins after the propagation gate, whereas online_elapsed_ms begins before RPC admission. This is sampled application-level progress, not an exact internal timer measurement.
progress_analysis.interpretation: Real height progression includes four absent round-zero proposer turns and additional rounds without a decision before the archived deciding round. The sum of round indices is not evidence that every preceding round formed a nil QC. The exact cause of every additional round is not established.

cases.finding: The fixture now distinguishes continued per-height progress from a stall: ninety seconds without common-height progress and a separate 240-second total fault-run ceiling. This avoids treating cumulative waits across rotating absent leaders and extra no-decision rounds as one stall, but does not demonstrate low fault latency or repair the first failed attempt retroactively. No production timer was changed.

cases.topology: Three unchanged original novovm-node OS processes plus one test-only Byzantine WSS/E2E peer, on one machine.
cases.finding: Three genuine signed A/A/B prevotes and nil precommits recover to an actual three-honest-signer decision, then preserve state across cold restarts and finalize a successor. The test peer signs only its own conflicting proposals; it neither manufactures honest votes nor supplies a QC. Restart is after confirmation, not a persistence-interruption or unknown-write-outcome test.

offline.accepted_scope: The unchanged eight-second propagation gate passes with the fourth validator absent; the three online original nodes decide thirty-two transactions, the returning fourth catches up, all four cold-restart and decide two successors with exact economics and archived QC verification. This is not low-latency or fault-capacity acceptance.

aab.accepted_scope: Actual honest A/A/B votes and nil precommits recover to a three-honest-signature decision, followed by confirmed-state cold restart and successor continuity. All topology and fault-injection limitations of the initial A/A/B case remain unchanged.

limitations: Initial eager-stats cases and final lazy-stats cases must retain their distinct binary identities.
The first new ninety-second failure remains a failure; no final-status capture proves its entire cause.
Functional progress and bounded propagation are verified, not low fault latency or fault-throughput capacity.
A/A/B uses three original executables and a test-only Byzantine peer, not four original executables.
No in-flight durable-write, journal power-loss or unknown-ACK fault was injected.
No four-machine, public-network, production or mainnet-performance acceptance is claimed.
